findings.title: RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE value changed from 4 to 3, reusing 4 for FEATURE_DISABLED
findings.body: CompatibilityResult.RECREATE_UPGRADE_EXIT_CODE was previously 4 and is now changed to 3, while the newly introduced FEATURE_DISABLED constant takes over the value 4. This silently changes the exit-code contract of the `update-compatibility check`/`metadata` CLI commands, which the accompanying documentation explicitly encourages users to script against ('the command's exit code can be used to determine the upgrade type'). Any existing automation or CI/CD pipeline built against the previously implemented exit code 4 for 'recreate upgrade required' will now receive exit code 3, and any logic checking for exit code 4 will misinterpret a 'feature disabled' result as 'recreate required'. This renumbering was not strictly necessary for the feature-flag work (a different unused exit code could have been chosen for FEATURE_DISABLED) and is not called out anywhere as an intentional breaking change.

findings.title: Feature-disabled guard is only tested for the metadata subcommand, not for check
findings.body: testFeatureNotEnabled only launches UpdateCompatibility.NAME + UpdateCompatibilityMetadata.NAME without the --features=rolling-updates flag, verifying the new 'feature disabled' error message. However, the identical feature-gating logic was also added to UpdateCompatibilityCheck.run() (quarkus/runtime/.../UpdateCompatibilityCheck.java), and there is no corresponding test verifying that running `update-compatibility check` without the rolling-updates feature enabled also prints the error and exits with CompatibilityResult.FEATURE_DISABLED. This leaves half of the newly added behavior completely untested.

findings.title: CAUTION about mandatory rolling-updates feature contradicts the default-behavior note that follows
findings.body: The CAUTION block placed immediately under '=== Managing Keycloak Operator Updates (Preview)' states unconditionally that 'the feature `rolling-updates` must be enabled. Otherwise, the {project_name} Operator will fail.' This reads as applying to the whole update-strategy feature area. However, the NOTE a few lines later explains that, by default (no explicit `update.strategy` set), the Operator falls back to mimicking 26.1-or-older behavior without requiring any feature flag — which matches the operator/src/test/java/.../UpgradeTest.java test setup, where the `updateStrategy == null` case never enables the rolling-updates feature and is expected to succeed. The documentation should clarify that the feature is only mandatory when explicitly configuring `spec.update.strategy`, not for the default/unset case, to avoid confusing operators into thinking the flag is always required.

findings.title: No test verifies the Operator fails when update.strategy is set without enabling the rolling-updates feature
findings.body: The documentation (docs/guides/operator/advanced-configuration.adoc) explicitly states that while the rolling-updates update-strategy feature is in preview, configuring `spec.update.strategy` without enabling the `rolling-updates` feature flag will cause the Operator to fail. createInitialDeployment() in this test only ever enables the feature together with a non-null update strategy, so this exact failure path (update.strategy set, feature not enabled) is never exercised. There is no negative test confirming the documented failure actually occurs, so a regression that silently ignores or mis-handles this combination would not be caught by this test suite.
